ai.literal: Whether they increase or whether they decrease, disease will cause, the treatise-authors' wind starting-with enumerated three.
ai.translation: The three elements starting with wind, enumerated by the learned, will cause disease if they increase or decrease.
ai.modern: மருத்துவ நூல்களை எழுதியவர்கள் வளி முதலாக எண்ணிய மூன்று கூறுகளும் தத்தம் அளவிலிருந்து மிகுந்தாலும் குறைந்தாலும் உடலில் நோயை உண்டாக்கும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet introduces the fundamental principle of health and disease. The learned authors of medical treatises have enumerated three bodily elements, beginning with wind. If these three elements either exceed or fall short of their natural balance, they will cause disease in the body. The word vali means wind, representing the first of the three vital forces.

ai.literal: Medicine as will not be needed for the body, what was eaten, what was digested having ensured if one eats.
ai.translation: No medicine is needed for the body if one eats only after ensuring that the food previously eaten has been fully digested.
ai.modern: முன்பு உண்ட உணவு முழுமையாகச் செரித்துவிட்டதா என்பதை உறுதிசெய்து பின்பு உண்டால், இந்த உடம்பிற்கு மருந்து என்று ஒன்று தேவையில்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet states a fundamental principle of health and digestion. The word 'யாக்கை' refers to the physical body, and 'அருந்தியது' means the food that was previously consumed. The term 'அற்றது' literally means 'that which is severed or ended', but here it specifically denotes the complete digestion of food. By 'போற்றி உணின்', the poet advises eating carefully, ensuring that the previous meal is fully digested before taking the next. If one follows this simple practice, the body will never require any medicine.

ai.literal: If digested, completely having known, let one eat; that [is the] body he-who-obtained long-time preserving way.
ai.translation: Let one eat after knowing fully that the previous meal has been digested. That is the way for one who has obtained a body to preserve it for a long time.
ai.modern: முன்பு உண்ட உணவு முழுமையாகச் செரித்துவிட்டதை அறிந்து அதன் பிறகு உண்ண வேண்டும். உடம்பைப் பெற்றவன் அதை நெடுங்காலம் வாழச் செய்யும் வழி அதுவே ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises eating only after ensuring the previous meal is completely digested. The word 'அற்றால்' means 'if it is digested', derived from the root 'அறு' meaning to sever or finish, while 'அற' emphasizes knowing this state 'completely'. 'உய்க்கும் ஆறு' refers to the way of maintaining or prolonging life. By following this simple dietary rule, a person who has been given a physical body can preserve it in good health for a long time.

ai.literal: what is digested having known, having adhered firmly, contrary things that are not, let one eat, completely having hungered.
ai.translation: Knowing that the previous meal has been digested and firmly adhering to that rule, let one eat foods that are not contrary to health, only after getting completely hungry.
ai.modern: முன்பு உண்ட உணவு செரித்ததை அறிந்து, அந்த முறையை உறுதியாகப் பின்பற்றி, உடலுக்கு மாறுபடாத உணவுகளை நன்கு பசித்த பிறகு உண்ண வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the fundamental rules for a healthy diet. The word 'அற்றது' (what is digested) emphasizes that one must wait until the previous meal is fully processed by the body. 'கடைப்பிடித்து' (adhering firmly) stresses the importance of making this a strict, unwavering habit. Finally, 'மாறு அல்ல' (things that are not contrary) and 'துவரப் பசித்து' (having hungered completely) advise eating only agreeable foods and only when true hunger sets in, ensuring optimal health.

ai.literal: Incompatibility without food having-refused if-eats, harm is-not to-life.
ai.translation: If one eats food that agrees with the body and deliberately refuses excess, there will be no harm to one's life.
ai.modern: உடலுக்கு ஒவ்வாத உணவுகளைத் தவிர்த்து, அளவோடு உண்டால், உயிருக்கு எந்த நோயும் வராது.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the dietary basis of good health. The phrase 'மாறுபாடு இல்லாத உண்டி' refers to food that does not conflict with one's bodily constitution or the seasons. 'மறுத்து உண்ணின்' means eating with restraint, deliberately refusing excess even when the food is agreeable. When a person follows these two rules—eating compatible food and practicing moderation—their life will be free from 'ஊறுபாடு' (harm or disease).

ai.literal: Limit having known with him who eats pleasure like will stand excessive great with him who has food disease.
ai.translation: Just as health stays with the man who eats knowing his limit, disease stays with the glutton who eats excessively.
ai.modern: தன் செரிமான அளவை அறிந்து உண்பவனிடம் இன்பம் நிலைத்திருப்பது போல, மிக அதிகமாக உண்பவனிடம் நோய் நிலைத்து நிற்கும்.
ai.explanation: The word iḻivu here means the limit or measure of one's digestion. The couplet draws a direct parallel between two states of being. Just as well-being and pleasure remain with the person who eats mindfully within their limits, illness takes up permanent residence in the person who consumes an excessive amount of food. The contrast between iṉpam (pleasure or health) and nōy (disease) highlights the physical consequences of dietary habits.

ai.literal: Fire measure without, he who knows not, excessively if eats, disease measure without will happen.
ai.translation: If one who does not know the measure of his digestive fire eats excessively, diseases will afflict him without measure.
ai.modern: ஒருவன் தன் பசியின் அளவை அறியாமல் அதிகமாக உண்டால், அவனுக்கு நோய்கள் அளவில்லாமல் ஏற்படும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses the word 'fire' (தீ) to represent hunger and the body's digestive power. It warns that a person must understand the limits of their digestion before consuming food. If one ignores this limit and eats excessively, the resulting diseases will also multiply without any limit. The parallel between eating beyond measure and suffering diseases beyond measure emphasizes the direct consequence of gluttony.

ai.literal: Disease having examined, disease cause having examined, that which mitigates method having examined, fittingly act.
ai.translation: Examine the disease, examine its root cause, examine the method that cures it, and then act effectively.
ai.modern: நோயை ஆராய்ந்து, அந்த நோய்க்கான காரணத்தை ஆராய்ந்து, அதனைத் தீர்க்கும் வழியையும் ஆராய்ந்து, பொருந்தும் படி மருத்துவம் செய்ய வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the systematic approach required to treat an illness. First, one must diagnose the disease itself, and then investigate its underlying cause. Next, one must determine the proper method to cure it. The word வாய் here means the way or method of treatment, rather than its common meaning of mouth. Finally, the treatment must be applied effectively and fittingly to ensure a complete cure.

ai.literal: The patient's measure and the disease's measure and the time, the learned one having considered, should act.
ai.translation: The learned physician should act only after considering the condition of the patient, the severity of the disease, and the season.
ai.modern: மருத்துவம் கற்ற மருத்துவர், நோயாளியின் உடல்நிலை, நோயின் தன்மை, மற்றும் காலம் ஆகியவற்றை நன்கு ஆராய்ந்த பிறகே மருத்துவச் செயல்களைச் செய்ய வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the three essential factors a physician must evaluate before treating a patient. 'உற்றான் அளவு' refers to the physical strength, age, and tolerance of the person suffering from the illness. 'பிணி அளவு' denotes the severity and stage of the disease itself. 'காலம்' indicates the time of year or the season, which affects both the body's condition and the efficacy of treatments. By carefully considering all three, the learned doctor ('கற்றான்') ensures the treatment is appropriate and effective.

ai.literal: Patient, healer, medicine, beside-goer, thus that part four divisions indeed medicine.
ai.translation: Medical practice consists of four parts: the patient, the healer, the medicine, and the attendant.
ai.modern: நோயாளி, மருத்துவர், மருந்து, அருகில் இருந்து உதவுபவர் என்று மருத்துவ முறை நான்கு பிரிவுகளை உடையதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the four essential components of medical treatment. The word 'maruntu' is used twice with two accepted senses: first meaning the physical medicine or drug, and finally referring to the entire medical system. It states that healing is a combined practice consisting of the patient, the doctor, the drug itself, and the attendant who stays beside the patient. All four divisions are necessary for a successful cure.
